exposure: Incidental p53 signature lesion in the fallopian tube
outcome: Malignancy (including ovarian or primary peritoneal cancer)
cohort: The study included 91 patients diagnosed with an incidental p53 signature lesion on final pathology from 2014 to 2022 at a large academic institution, after excluding those with established ovarian cancer or a high-risk history.
finding: The diagnosis of an incidental p53 signature was not associated with any primary peritoneal or ovarian cancer diagnoses during the follow-up period.
